question: A shopkeeper marks the price of an article at ₹5,180. Find the cost price if after allowing a discount of 31% he still gains 5% on the cost price.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct relation between **Cost Price (CP)** and **Marked Price (MP)**: **CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%)**.

CP / 5,180 = (100 − 31) / (100 + 5) ⇒ CP / 5,180 = 69 / 105.

CP = (69 / 105) × 5,180.

CP = (23 / 35) × 5,180 ⇒ CP = 23 × 148.

CP = 3,404.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,404.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **Marked Price (MP)** = ₹5,180, **Discount** = 31%, **Gain** = 5%.
Formulas: SP = MP × (100 − D%) / 100 | CP = SP × 100 / (100 + P%).
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/84f64c4808d93938a8cdc398a241056c97d706e45f5d19d69f5bcfbb4140e720.png] 
⇒ Calculate **Selling Price (SP)**: SP = 5,180 × (100 − 31) / 100.
⇒ SP = 5,180 × 0.69 = 3,574.2.
⇒ Calculate **Cost Price (CP)**: CP = 3,574.2 × 100 / (100 + 5).
⇒ CP = 3,574.2 ÷ 1.05 = 3,404.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,404.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. SP = MP − Discount.

Profit and CP Relationship

Profit is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)**. SP = CP + Profit.
